title: A Blanket of Darkness
text: A thick, suffocating blanket of darkness envelops the entire globe. Sunlight cannot reach the forest floor for months.
nxt: Without sunlight, green leaves wither and photosynthesis grinds to a halt. Herbivorous dinosaurs starve as their lush pastures disappear.

nxt: This means offspring do not depend immediately on foraging outside. Parents can shelter their vulnerable babies inside protected dens.

prev: Meanwhile, the rise of Panama redirects major ocean currents worldwide.

title: The Rift Valley
text: The world enters the Pliocene epoch, drifting toward an even colder regime.
nxt: In East Africa, the drying climate creates dramatic ecological shifts. The great Rift Valley deepens, carving rugged cliffs and deep depressions.

title: Standing Up
text: According to a leading hypothesis, there is only one way to reach the next patch of fruiting trees: cross open ground.
nxt: Crossing the grass on all fours leaves you blind to stalking predators. A leopard can easily ambush an ape crawling through tall yellow stems.

title: Free Hands

nxt: Cool breezes can circulate freely around your heated torso. Most importantly of all, your two front hands are completely free.

title: First Steps and Stone Edges
text: Somewhere between six and eight million years ago, by most estimates, the human lineage splits from the one that leads to chimpanzees.
nxt: Bipedal walking is not merely a different posture; it opens a new path.

title: Footprints and Lucy
text: In Tanzania, at a place called Laetoli, a trail of footprints more than three and a half million years old was pressed into volcanic ash.
nxt: They were made by upright walkers.

title: Footprints and Lucy

nxt: And in Ethiopia, a famous skeleton nicknamed Lucy, about three point two million years old, shows a body built for walking on two legs.

title: The Great Ice Age
text: As the Pliocene yields to the Pleistocene, the planet enters a deep freeze. Massive sheets of glacial ice advance from the polar north.
nxt: Gigantic glaciers grind across continents, retreating and advancing in cyclic rhythms.

title: Giants of the Ice
text: Woolly mammoths grow dense coats of shaggy fur and layers of insulating fat. Saber-toothed cats stalk heavy prey across wind-swept mammoth steppes.
nxt: Giant ground sloths weighing several tonnes lumber through forests, stripping branches bare.

title: The Gift of Fire
text: They do not possess thick fur coats to shield against howling blizzards. They do not have elongated ivory tusks or razor-sharp fangs for defense.
nxt: Instead, they possess something far more adaptable than physical armor. They learn to harness the dancing flame of fire.

title: Our Own Species
text: Our own species, Homo sapiens, appears in Africa roughly three hundred thousand years ago, and later spreads across the world.
nxt: We are not alone at first. Neanderthals share Europe and western Asia with us for thousands of years, and many people today still carry a small amount of Neanderthal DNA.

nxt: Some of those paintings, like the ones in Chauvet Cave in France, are more than thirty thousand years old.

title: Villages and Cities
text: In the Middle East, people farm wheat and barley, and in China, rice. Permanent walls rise from sun-baked mud and woven reed mats.
nxt: Surplus grain is stored in clay jars, guarding against unexpected famine. For the first time, not everyone must spend daylight hunting.

title: Writing Begins
text: In Mesopotamia, more than five thousand years ago, writing emerges as small incisions on soft clay tablets to count sheep and grain.
nxt: Recorded history begins, a mere blink against the vast backdrop of deep time. Think back to that dark morning sixty-six million years ago.

nxt: They did not know that their distant lineage would cross stormy oceans.

title: Your Hands Again
text: Every challenge the planet delivered became an invitation to adapt. When the world froze, mammals grew thick fur and forged social bonds.
nxt: When the forests vanished, our ancestors stood tall on two feet to see farther. Now, take another look at your hands resting quietly before you.
